chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mufaddal ibn Umar,al ibn Umar, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and we mentioned the deeds. So I said, 'How weak are my deeds.' He said, 'Hush! Seek forgiveness of Allah.' Then he said to me, 'Indeed, a little deed with piety is better than a lot of deeds without piety.' I said, 'How can there be a lot without piety?' He said, 'Yes, like the man who feeds his food, is kind to his neighbors, and eases his burden (for others). So when the door of the prohibited is raised for him, he enters into it. So this is the deed without piety. And the other one may be such that he does not have much, but when the door of the prohibited is raised for him, he does not enter into it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a little deed with piety and a lot of deeds without piety?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that piety (taqwa) is the essential filter for the acceptance of deeds, illustrating that even abundant acts of charity and neighborliness are nullified if tainted by consuming haram wealth. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the purity of source (mal al-halal vs. mal al-haram) as a prerequisite for spiritual validity, rather than mere quantitative accumulation of rituals.
